summary: Converts non-time-sliced input into a time slice from the previous cooked frame to the current frame using hold or interpolation, smoothing skipped-frame control data.
key_concepts: Time Slice CHOP outputs a CHOP time slice covering samples between the previous cooked frame and the current frame.
It smooths input that is only sampled when TouchDesigner cooks or draws, filling skipped frames before downstream CHOPs such as Record, Gesture, or Lag.
The output keeps the input channel names and count while changing the frame range to the current time-slice region.
Hold mode repeats the current value through the slice, while Linear mode interpolates between the last cooked value and current value.
Trim mode outputs the input trimmed to the current time-slice range.
Quaternion Blend uses quaternion interpolation for channels tagged as rotation channels.

key_params.name: hold
key_params.note: Hold current value across the time slice

key_params.name: linear
key_params.note: Interpolate from last cook value to current value

key_params.name: trim
key_params.note: Trim input to current time-slice region

common_gotchas: Channel names and count do not change; only the output frame range becomes the current time slice.
Useful before Record CHOP, Gesture CHOP, and Lag CHOP when input is sampled only on cooked frames.
Linear mode interpolates values between the last cook and current cook; Hold mode repeats current values across the slice.
If the input lies outside the current time-slice region, extend conditions may be sampled.
Do not use Time Slice CHOP when full static channel history is required.
